bug_semantics: The Markdown and PDF evaluation-export routes authorized only access to the conversion, then build_evaluation_report() selected every non-deleted evaluation comment without applying the already-established per-comment privacy rule. On a public conversion, any viewer, including an anonymous viewer, could therefore export a private evaluation comment belonging to another author and receive both its content and the author's first name; only the conversion owner, comment author, or an administrator should see such a comment.
flaw_origin: Direct feature introduction in c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f: the same one-parent commit created both export routes and build_evaluation_report(), whose comment loop appended every selected evaluation comment without a visibility check. Later conversion-model renames and refactors preserved that omission; blame immediately before the fix still traces the query, loop, author, and content lines to c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f.
evidence: Bundle advisory GHSA-VRRH-VGMQ-M54X/CVE-2026-73140 identifies the missing comment-level authorization in build_evaluation_report() and references fix 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42. Reproduce the vulnerable path with `git show c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate.py website/web/evaluate/evaluate_core.py`: the new unauthenticated Markdown/PDF routes permit every viewer of a public conversion, call build_evaluation_report(convert_id) without an actor, and the new report builder queries all is_evaluation=True, is_deleted=False comments before unconditionally appending author and content.

The privacy contract predated the export feature. `git grep -n -A18 -B5 '_can_see_comment' c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f -- website/web/convert/convert_core.py` shows that normal comment retrieval hid a private comment on a public conversion from everyone except the conversion owner, comment author, or admin, while the export builder did not call that rule. `git grep -n -A12 -B5 'is_private' c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f -- website/db_class/db.py` confirms the Comment.is_private field.

Smallest-BIC and parent-absence checks: `git log --all --reverse --format='%H %P %ai %s' -S'build_evaluation_report' -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate_core.py website/web/evaluate/evaluate.py`, the corresponding `-S'eval_comments_raw'`, and `-S'export_evaluation_markdown'` all first return c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f with sole parent 6cd6133775a573dd93409af9b120cbb12b647988. `git diff --unified=8 6cd6133775a573dd93409af9b120cbb12b647988 c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate.py website/web/evaluate/evaluate_core.py` directly shows both export endpoints and the entire unfiltered report function as additions; the parent has both files but neither added block. The commit is the direct feature commit, not a move, merge, revert, release commit, or identifiable squash aggregate, so no member decomposition is applicable.

Refactor cross-check: `git blame -L 449,525 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42^ -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate_core.py` attributes the vulnerable evaluation-comment query, loop, author lookup, content append, and most of the report function to c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f despite later identifier changes; `git blame -L 245,292 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42^ -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate.py` likewise traces the export endpoints to it.

Direct closing fix: `git show --format=fuller 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42` shows parent 06d408e3496fdfc31da22d7b2b427434c67eae94, moves the existing rule to website/lib/access.py as can_see_comment(), passes the concrete requesting actor from both export routes into build_evaluation_report(), and skips each comment for which access.can_see_comment(actor, c, conversion) is false. `git grep -n -E 'build_evaluation_report\(conversion_id\)|for c in eval_comments_raw|eval_comments.append' 06d408e3496fdfc31da22d7b2b427434c67eae94 -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate.py website/web/evaluate/evaluate_core.py` confirms the immediate fix parent still called the actorless builder and appended the unfiltered rows; `git log -S'build_evaluation_report(conversion_id, actor'` and `git log -S'access.can_see_comment(actor'` identify 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42 as the direct closing commit.

Release boundary: `git tag --contains c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f --sort=version:refname` returns v1.4 and v1.5, while `git tag --contains 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42 --sort=version:refname` returns only v1.5. `git merge-base --is-ancestor c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f v1.3` exits 1. Thus v1.3 is unaffected, v1.4 is the affected release, and v1.5 is the first fixed release; the untagged vulnerable interval is c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f through the parent of 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f`/`git show --format=raw --no-patch c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f` shows author and committer `ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>`, one parent, the subject `add: [MarkDown/PDF] new way to see the evaluation of a convert`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot trailer/identity. Therefore there is no BIC commit-object AI signal; later commits and the fix are irrelevant to the AI verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is a missing object-level authorization check inside a newly introduced export aggregation path, not a defect created by later renames or by the fix. c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f is the first and smallest public-history commit that adds the reachable export endpoints and the unfiltered comment aggregation, and its immediate parent lacks both. The direct fix 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42 closes the exact path by sharing the established comment-visibility predicate and supplying the requesting actor. Tag ancestry fixes the released range at v1.4 only, with v1.5 first fixed. Because the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no qualifying AI marker or bot identity, the required BIC-only judgment is NOT_AI.
